chunks: Hamzah ibn Humran narrated; he said: Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said:

“My descendant will be killed in the land of Khurasan, in a city called Tus. Whoever visits him there, recognizing his right, I will take him by the hand on the Day of Judgment and admit him into Paradise, even if he is among the people of major sins.”

He said: I said, “May I be your ransom, and what is recognition of his right?” He said: “That he knows that he is an Imam whose obedience is divinely mandated, a stranger, a martyr. Whoever visits him recognizing his right, Allah, Mighty and Exalted, gives him the reward of seventy martyrs from among those who were martyred before the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله on true faith.”

key_terms.أَجْرَ سَبْعِينَ شَهِيدًا: the reward equivalent to seventy martyrs
key_terms.إِمَامٌ مُفْتَرَضُ الطَّاعَةِ: an Imam whose obedience is obligatory by divine command
key_terms.حَقِّهِ: his due right, meaning his true divinely established rank and authority
key_terms.غَرِيبٌ: a stranger, one away from his homeland and people
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Resurrection and final reckoning

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the Imam in Tus while recognizing his right?
ai.summary: This hadith foretells the martyrdom of a descendant of the Imam in Tus, understood in Shia tradition as Imam al-Rida عليه السلام, and highlights the immense merit of visiting him with proper recognition of his divinely ordained status. It links ziyārah with ma'rifah of the Imam, intercession on the Day of Judgment, and a great reward in the afterlife.
